If your Expensify renewal is on the calendar, or you're budgeting expense software for 300 people, the pricing page won't give you a defensible number. Expensify pricing headlines lead with $5 per member a month for Collect and "as low as $9" for Control. The billing documentation tells a fuller story, with Control at $18 per committed member and $36 for each active member above the commitment.


Those figures describe the same plans under different conditions. What you pay depends on the plan your ERP requires and whether you commit annually. It also depends on active member growth and how much approved spend runs on the Expensify Card. At 300 seats on Control Annual, card share alone moves the bill between $5,400 and $2,700 a month.


That spread is why the per-seat headline is a poor budgeting tool for a mid-size team. Every Expensify rate here is as of November 2026 and in USD. Your own quote may differ, so treat every figure as a starting point for the conversation with your account rep.


## Key Takeaways


-


Collect costs $5 per unique member monthly, pay-per-use only, and Control Annual is $18 per committed member plus $36 per active member above.


-


Control's "as low as $9" requires the full 50% Expensify Card discount, measured against all approved USD expenses in the workspace.


-


NetSuite and Sage Intacct integrations require the Control plan, while QuickBooks Online runs on Collect.


-


An Annual subscription size can rise mid-term but can't come down until renewal.


-


On published rates, 300 committed Control Annual seats cost $64,800 a year before any card discount.


## What is Expensify pricing for each plan?


Expensify has three workspace plans. Submit is free, and Collect is $5 per member monthly. Control bills $18 per committed member or $36 per active member, and Control Annual drops to "as low as $9" with the Expensify Card.


[Expensify's pricing page](https://www.expensify.com/pricing) leads with the $5 Collect rate and an "as low as $9" Control price. The billing help center prices Control Annual at $18 per committed member and pay-per-use at $36 per active member. Both pages are accurate. The $9 is the $18 rate after the maximum 50% card discount, so the two pages describe one plan at two different card shares.

Taxes aren't included and are "calculated separately based on your billing location and tax status." Expensify does not publish a seat minimum. Two discounts are built into the published rates. The annual commitment halves the pay-per-use seat price, and the card discount can halve it again. Ask for the discount schedule in writing before you compare quotes.


### Is Expensify really free?


Expensify is free for individuals on its[Submit workspace](https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/getting-started/Submit-Workspace) , where employees can scan receipts and submit reports at no cost. It isn't free for a company that runs expenses as a process.


According to Expensify's help center, "Premium features are not included in a Submit workspace," including approvals, payments, company cards, and accounting integrations. For a finance team, free ends at the first approval chain. Without approvals, nobody signs off before reimbursement. Without accounting sync, someone moves every approved report into the ledger by hand.


That manual review and reconciliation time is the cost an expense tool is meant to remove. It's also the number to measure in your own close. If you're tightening policy too, settle[what goes in an expense report](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-report) first, because a plan only enforces the rules you write.


### What happened to the old Collect price?


If your organization created its first workspace before April 1, 2025, it stays on legacy Collect pricing, which bills differently from the current $5 plan.


Per[Expensify's billing documentation](https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/billing-and-subscriptions/Billing-Overview) , legacy Annual Collect costs "$5 per member included in your subscription size/month, plus $10 per active member above your subscription size/month." Legacy pay-per-use Collect is $10 per active member monthly. Current Collect bills $5 per unique member, and "Collect Workspaces are available only with a Pay-per-use subscription."


The counting basis changed too. Current Collect bills unique members, while the legacy plan bills active members. Older reviews of Expensify often quote the legacy $10 figure as if it still applied to new accounts. Confirm which pricing your account sits on before you set it beside any other vendor's number.


## How does Expensify bill a company in practice?


Control bills one of two ways. Annual commits you to a seat count at $18 each plus $36 per active member above it, and pay-per-use charges $36 per active member. Expensify Card usage can cut either by up to half.


### What is the difference between annual and pay-per-use?


Annual is a 12-month commitment to a subscription size, and only Control workspaces can use it. Pay-per-use bills each month for active members at $36, with no commitment.


Expensify's documentation is direct about the lock. "You can increase your subscription size at any time." However, "You can't decrease your subscription size until your subscription renews." Every seat included in the subscription size bills at $18, whether or not that member files an expense. Active members above the commitment bill at $36.


That combination is the seat-commitment trap. The commitment can't come down until renewal, while overage runs at $36, double the $18 committed rate. Size to today's headcount and every hire above it costs $36 a month. Size for next year's growth and you pay $18 for seats nobody uses yet.


The fix I'd push for at any renewal is to size the commitment to your trailing average of monthly active submitters rather than HR headcount. HR headcount counts people who never file an expense, and it misses the contractors who do. Then get Expensify's definition of an "active member" in writing, because that definition decides how much overage you'll pay.


Pay-per-use costs twice as much per seat at list. It still suits seasonal or uncertain headcount, because nothing you commit to in January follows you into a slow quarter.


### How does the Expensify card discount work?


Control Annual workspaces earn up to a 50% subscription discount. The discount rises with the share of approved USD expenses that run on the Expensify Card.


The[Expensify Card page](https://use.expensify.com/company-credit-card) states, "Put at least half your spend on the Expensify Card and get 50% off your Expensify subscription." The billing documentation adds that the discount uses "all approved USD expenses in your Workspace during the billing month." It "increases proportionally, up to a maximum of 50%."


The denominator is the detail most buyers miss. Every approved USD expense counts, including mileage, per diem, and out-of-pocket reimbursements that never touch a card. A field service team with heavy reimbursed travel can run every card purchase on the Expensify Card and still miss the full discount.


The card itself has no fees, according to Expensify. It pays 1% cash back, or 2% when spend tops $250,000 a month across cards, and that applies to USD purchases on US cards only. The card draws on the connected bank account and can't carry a balance, so plan for card spend to leave operating cash as it posts.


Because the savings depend on card share, your card policy carries the discount. Clear[card controls and spend policies](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/card-controls-spend-policies) decide which expenses land on the card and which come back as reimbursements.

Some costs sit outside the subscription line. Expensify Travel charges a fee per trip.[Expensify's travel fee breakdown](https://help.expensify.com/articles/travel/getting-started/How-to-Get-Expensify-Travel-Support-from-an-Agent.html) lists $15 for a self-serve trip and $25 for an assisted trip. "The assisted trip fee only applies once per trip."


Those fees grow with every trip your people book. According to the[GBTA 2026 Business Travel Index](https://gbta.org/research/2026-business-travel-index-bti/) , global business travel spending will reach a record $1.71 trillion in 2026, across approximately 1.84 billion trips. A travel-heavy 300-person team should budget trip fees as their own line.


When you set these numbers beside other[expense report software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-report-software) , carry the trip fees and any card-share shortfall as separate lines. A per-seat comparison alone hides both.


### Which features push you from Collect to Control?


Usually the ERP. Expensify lists the Control plan as a requirement to[connect NetSuite](https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/connections/netsuite/Connect-To-NetSuite) , its[Sage Intacct integration](https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/connections/sage-intacct/Connect-to-Sage-Intacct) "is only available on the Control plan," and[QuickBooks Online needs Collect](https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/connections/quickbooks-online/Connect-to-QuickBooks-Online) .


Multiple approval levels and rules are Control features too. For a mid-size company, that ERP line matters more than any feature. A multi-entity NetSuite shop is a Control customer on day one, and the $5 headline never applies to it. Expensify's NetSuite guide also calls for one Expensify workspace per NetSuite subsidiary, so plan the setup entity by entity.


Collect fits a team that closes in QuickBooks Online and runs one simple approval path. Once you add a second entity or a multi-level approval chain, you're pricing Control.


The plan choice doesn't change what employees do most often, which is get paid back. Test how any[expense reimbursement software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-reimbursement-software) handles mileage and payout timing before you choose a tier.


## Is Expensify worth the price for a mid-size finance team?


Often yes for card-heavy teams that can reach the full discount. The case is weaker for reimbursement-heavy teams, and on either plan the subscription doesn't touch supplier payments or rebate economics.


Start with what Expensify does well. Receipt scanning is free even on the Submit workspace, its card handles auto-coding and receipt matching, and the card requires no deposits, personal guarantees, or credit checks. For a team that lives on the card, those strengths are worth paying for.


The control case is real too. According to the[ACFE 2026 Report to the Nations](https://www.acfe.com/-/media/files/acfe/pdfs/rttn/2026/2026-report-to-the-nations.pdf) , expense reimbursement schemes appeared in 13% of 2,402 occupational fraud cases, with a $36,000 median loss. Those schemes typically lasted 18 months before detection. Shortening that lag is the job of approval workflows and[expense fraud detection and prevention](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-fraud-detection-prevention) routines.


Cards are also spreading faster than the tools that reconcile them. The[Center 2024 Annual Trends Survey](https://getcenter.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Center-2024-Trends-Survey.pdf) is vendor research covering 200+ US finance leaders at SMEs. According to Center's 2024 survey, corporate card distribution grew 46% over 2022, while expense tool implementation rose 2% in 2023. Treat a vendor survey as directional. The gap still matches what month-end looks like when card lines arrive faster than[credit card reconciliation software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/credit-card-reconciliation-software) can clear them.


Scale puts the subscription in proportion. According to the[Nilson Report on US commercial cards](https://nilsonreport.com/articles/us-commercial-cards-amex-mastercard-and-visa-in-2024/) , Issue 1298, US commercial card purchase volume was $2.230 trillion in 2024, up 4.5% over 2023. An expense subscription governs the employee slice of that volume.


Supplier invoices paid by check and ACH are spend that earns no card rebate. An expense subscription doesn't reach it.


One question stays open. Is the card discount a saving or a switching cost? That depends on whether the Expensify Card is the card you'd choose anyway, and only your card terms can answer it. Weigh it either way when you build a shortlist of the[best expense management software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/best-expense-management-software) .


### How does Expensify compare with SAP Concur on price?


Expensify publishes its rates. For Concur Expense, ask SAP Concur for a written quote on the same seat count, billing basis, and integration tier.


That turns the comparison into a matter of asking the same questions twice. Ask each vendor for its overage rate and for how it counts an active user, because a per-seat figure means little without those two answers.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much does Expensify cost per month?


As of November 2026, Collect is $5 per unique member monthly. Control is $18 per committed member on Annual or $36 per active member on pay-per-use. The Expensify Card can bring Control Annual as low as $9 per member. If you're budgeting a mid-size team, our team can run that math against your actual card and supplier spend.


### Is Expensify free for small businesses?


Submit is free for individual members, but it leaves out approvals, payments, company cards, and accounting integrations. Most businesses with a manager approving expenses need Collect at $5 per unique member, and a team closing in NetSuite or Sage Intacct needs Control. Smaller teams are welcome at Corpay too, and we can show you how a card program grows with you.


### Does the Expensify card cost anything?


No, Expensify states there are no fees or costs associated with the card, which is issued by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. It pays 1% cash back, or 2% above $250,000 in monthly spend across cards. Its share of approved USD expenses also lowers Control Annual pricing. If you want to weigh that against rebates on supplier payments, we'll walk through your spend mix with you.


### Can you lower your Expensify seat count mid-contract?


Not on an Annual subscription. Expensify says you can increase your subscription size at any time but can't decrease it until renewal. Active members above the commitment bill at $36. Size the commitment to your trailing active submitters, and talk with our team before renewal if you're weighing a switch.


### Who owns Expensify?


Expensify, Inc. is a public company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker EXFY, according to[Expensify investor relations](https://investors.expensify.com/) . Its shareholders own it. If your question is really about who should own your card program, Corpay's specialists are happy to compare options with you.
